name: commander-excess-arguments-error-by-default-i18next-parser
behavioral_change: In commander v_new (13.0.0), the default of `allowExcessArguments` changed from true to false: v_old (12.1.0) left extra command-arguments in `program.args` for the downstream to use, whereas v13 rejects the same command line with `error: too many arguments. Expected 0 arguments but got N.` and exit code 1. Option declarations, `program.parse` and the reading of `program.args` are unchanged and no exception or deprecation warning is raised.
downstream_effect: i18next-parser's bin/cli.js declares only `.option()` entries and reads file globs from `program.args` after `program.parse(process.argv)`, so after the upgrade every invocation with a glob on the command line exits with `too many arguments` and four tests in test/cli/cli.test.js fail with `ExecaError` or string assertions. No stack frame falls in bin/cli.js and the output never names the commander package; the file name appears only inside the echoed child command line.
reference_fix: The reference fix adds one line to bin/cli.js, calling `program.allowExcessArguments()` after the option declarations and before `program.parse(process.argv)`.
documented_in: The commander v13.0.0 release notes announce the breaking change in the Changed section and, under Migration Tips (Excess command-arguments), show the error text and two code blocks, one of which uses `program.allowExcessArguments();` exactly as in the reference fix. The Readme.md of the same version also states that `.allowExcessArguments()` suppresses the check.
failing_tests: test/cli/cli.test.js :: CLI > works when no input found
